name: cg-omniverse
description: CG-Omniverse: the CG area's Android app behind the SuperApp's Cloud > Lnktree row. Three pages on the shared bottom nav: Galaxy (opens the CG Galaxy web app, read from the registry), Game Store and VR Store (planned, greyed). The pages are declared in build.json::ui and drawn by declared kinds; the address of Galaxy is read at build time from the SuperApp's own declarations, none is typed here.

android._doc_application_id: The Lnktree family (1_cicd/src/data/app-families.json): com.diegonmarcos. + the app's name with its separators dropped, as cloudcalc / cloudsearch for the Cloud family.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.
auto_update._doc_enabled: Off because this app compiles no libs:updater: the Store updates it, as it does Cloud Calc and Cloud Search.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph; settings.gradle iterates it. No `logic` lib is compiled in (lib-classes L4): the Store installs and updates this app, as it does Cloud Calc.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which makes this app a fleet mesh member with the debug API.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:bottomnav._doc: #868 the fleet's NavDecl (ui.bottom_nav/ui.sections baked into BuildConfig), the top-bar scaffold's drawer and the scroll collapse, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:perms._doc: #1360 the permission contract (libs:perms): Configs > General > Perms (AppPermsSection, linked by libs:ui-nav-bars), first run (PermsFirstRun), PermsGate, and the state provider helper apps are read through.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds.

unit._doc: This app's JVM suite in app/src/test: Pages (the entries of a declared stack and where each leads) and Holdings (the local list).

ui._doc: #868 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl) of CG-Omniverse: the sections on the bottom bar in order, and a hidden About behind the gear of the first row. #1335 ui.stacks[<section>] is the page of that section: a list of entries drawn by declared KIND (Pages.kt: entry, section_title, holdings, about). An `entry` has a title, a one-line subtitle and ONE declared source for its target: `site` (the label of a link of aa_cloud-superapp/data/linktree.json), `registry` (a code of aa_cloud-superapp/build.json ui.app_urls.registry_sites) or `repo` + `path` (a repo under ui.app_urls.repo_base); app/build.gradle resolves them at BUILD time from the SuperApp's own declarations (fails if one does not resolve) and bakes UI_TARGETS_B64, so no address is typed in this file or in Kotlin. A `planned` entry has a note and no source and is drawn greyed. No price, rate or chart is declared: nothing real to show yet.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: The CG area's galaxy, games and VR
about.description: CG-Omniverse is the CG area's app, opened from the SuperApp's Cloud ▸ Lnktree row. Its Galaxy page opens the CG Galaxy web app, whose address is read at build time from the fleet registry rather than typed into the app; the Game Store and VR Store pages are planned and shown greyed until they exist. It exists so each area of the owner's work has its own entry point on the phone, drawn by the same shared navigation as every fleet app.

about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
